answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before transacting, like a ship paying to dock at a wharf. The stake stays locked for a long window, so spawning thousands of fake identities ties up real capital per identity and makes a sybil flood expensive. Honest agents earn the nectar of a reputation dividend that grows only with time and successful trades, while bad actors forfeit stake and standing. Newcomers begin in a low-trust meadow of small deals and graduate to larger ones only after a clean history, forcing an attacker to pay heavily or wait months to matter.
